runner.post_run_changes: The historical run used a top-level datasets field. The retained runner now uses the validated options.datasets contract and was additionally hardened for plan-only defaults, a bounded explicit live budget, failure handling, and persisted-error privacy. The historical aggregate was not rerun, so the generated_with hash remains the provenance for those counts.

1d.meaning: provider predicate request for yesterday only

test_design.maxDate_semantic_effect_scope: Denver city/state control for both predicates; not independently proven for every match or geography
test_design.polygon_geography: Equal nominal 5mi x 5mi center square (25 sq mi)
test_design.predicate_relationship: Intel and Sale are alternative filters on the same Property Search endpoint; Lookup is a separate targeted enrichment endpoint.

lookup_metric_definitions.matched: Historical runner field meaning: an HTTP-successful Lookup response yielded an extractable first row; record identity was not independently verified.
lookup_metric_definitions.positive_field_delta: Historical runner field meaning: the Lookup populated-value count exceeded Search in an 11-field monitored vector; this was not a full field-by-field payload comparison.

max_date_semantic_control.design: Held minDate at 2026-06-25 and compared maxDate 2026-07-01 with maxDate 2026-07-08.
max_date_semantic_control.interpretation: Both Denver city/state predicates lost exactly one candidate when maxDate moved before the returned 2026-07-02 sample date. This demonstrates a semantic upper-bound effect in that control, not universal enforcement.

polygon_density_per_nominal_sq_mile.meaning: BatchData provider-side candidate count divided by nominal polygon area; not external sales recall.

returned_date_validation.known_stale_sample: One Sacramento Search sample exposed 2012-09-20 while passing the provider 14-day predicate.

conclusion.yesterday: Neither Search predicate returned a candidate for the one-day request in any of 25 polygon or city/state tests; hidden qualifying dates mean this is not an external deed-ground-truth statement.
conclusion.two_day: Intel returned one city/state candidate in Orlando; Sale returned zero. Search exposed no sale date, and its Lookup row exposed no monitored Intel date, type, or deed history and no increase in monitored populated-field count.
conclusion.seven_day: Intel returned two city/state candidates across Orlando and Denver; Sale returned the Denver candidate only. Polygon counts were zero for both.
conclusion.fourteen_day: Intel was equal to or more inclusive than Sale, but returned fields still did not expose intel.lastSoldDate or explicit SFR metadata.
conclusion.production_recommendation: Independently paginate the qualified intel.lastSoldDate and sale.lastSaleDate streams, de-duplicate their record-level union, and retain exact job-scoped R2, estimated-value, listing-exclusion, polygon, and date provenance. Neither predicate is an external truth set; any contradictory returned field still rejects the record.

billing.note: HTTP requests are counted, but provider credit charges are not inferred.

limitations: This measures two filters on BatchData Property Search plus targeted Lookup enrichment; it does not measure external MLS/deed penetration.
The polygon universe uses nominal 25-square-mile center-city rectangles; city/state controls use provider-defined municipal matching.
Results are a snapshot for one API key/account contract on 2026-07-09, not a permanent availability guarantee.
Address-level Search comparison is capped at five records per predicate per sampled city and is not a full-universe join.
Count requests used the basic dataset while field-audit samples used expanded datasets, so sample eligibility/order is not assumed to reproduce the count universe.
Lookup comparison is capped at two union records per sampled city; extractable first rows were not independently identity-matched.
The monitored Lookup population metric covers 11 fields and is not a full field-by-field diff.
No property addresses, owner data, API keys, provider error bodies, or raw provider payloads are retained.
The Denver semantic control demonstrated an upper-bound effect for both predicates, but hidden date fields prevent proof for every provider match and geography.
Because raw responses were not retained, the audit validates this derived JSON and runner logic rather than the underlying provider payloads.
